title: Adaptive canary and rollback decision engine for heterogeneous deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an adaptive decision engine that drives canary rollouts, A/B experiments, and automated rollback across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. The engine will translate high-level rollout policies into environment-specific runtime configs, score canaries using both reliability and quality signals, throttle or shadow traffic when metrics are incomplete, and trigger deterministic rollbacks when regression thresholds are exceeded. This ticket covers the design, runtime adaptor implementation, end-to-end tests, and product integration points with Console rollouts and metrics backends.
background: We have multiple tickets addressing traffic splitting, rollout policies and SLO-aware routing, but customers still struggle to get consistent behavior across Hosted, Dedicated and Private. Key gaps: 1) policy parity often breaks because Private deployments lack the same metric ingestion or control-plane reachability, 2) rollbacks are either too eager (causing flapping) or too late (exposing customers to bad model outputs), and 3) A/B experiments need deterministic weighting and measurement windows across heterogeneous infra. This work aims to provide a single decision layer that adapts policies by environment but yields predictable developer UX.
constraints:
- Private installs may have delayed metric ingestion (up to minutes) and no direct control-plane mutation abilities.
- Dedicated pools expose differing autoscaling semantics and capacity constraints.
- Hosted must support low-latency automated rollback (sub-minute) without affecting global tenant isolation.
- Any design must respect customer-specified data residency and KMS constraints.
- No additional infra that requires elevated customer permissions in Private (no extra agents unless optional).
proposed_solution: 1) Policy DSL: extend rollout policy to include environment profiles (hosted/dedicated/private) and fallback strategies. 2) Decision Engine: a stateless service that consumes metric streams and policy, outputs traffic directives (percentages, shadow rates, throttle). 3) Scoring: compute a composite canary score from latency, error-rate, token-quality regression metrics (embedding drift / hallucination score) and business KPIs. 4) Adapters: small runtime adaptors for Dedicated and Private that map directives to available mechanisms (route tables, iptables for shadowing, control-plane mutators). 5) Safe rollback: hysteresis + graded rollback (reduce traffic in steps) and automatic pause if metrics are noisy. 6) Telemetry: emit decision events and rationale for Console audit and human review.
acceptance_criteria: Policy DSL supports environment profile and at least two fallback strategies (model-variant, region-shift)
Decision Engine publishes directives with stable schema and documented rationale events
Adapters for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private implemented and tested in staging
E2E scenario: introduce a synthetic regression and observe automated graded rollback within configured thresholds in Hosted
For Private, when metric latency > configured threshold, engine should switch to conservative mode (shadow-only or reduced canary) rather than full promotion
Console shows per-canary score, contributing signals, and provides one-click manual override
Automated tests covering A/B weighting determinism and rollback hysteresis (no flapping in 3 repeated failure windows)
implementation_steps: Design: finalize Policy DSL with PM and Compliance (1 week)
Prototype: implement scoring library and decision engine (2 weeks)
Adapters: implement hosted adapter (traffic split), dedicated adapter (pool routing), private adapter (sidecar/iptables option) (2 weeks)
Integration: hook decision events to Console and metrics backends; add audit trail (3 days)
Test: build synthetic failure harnesses to validate rollback and hysteresis (1 week)
Canary: run limited internal rollout with staging workloads, gather feedback (3 days)
Ship: enable behind feature flag and run gradual ramp (monitor for 2 weeks)
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring functions (latency, error-rate, quality regression)
Simulation tests: run 1000 synthetic canaries with mixed signal noise and validate expected decisions
E2E hosted smoke with true traffic shadowing in dev environment
Dedicated pool test: ensure adapter respects pool capacity and doesn't overcommit GPUs
Private regression: simulate delayed metrics (30s-120s) and verify conservative fallback
Chaos: induce intermittent metric gaps to validate no-flap rollback behavior
monitoring_playbook:
- Primary signals: 95/99 P50 latency, request error rate, token rejection rate, quality regression score by eval prompt set.
- Decision events are tagged with canary_id, policy_id, score_breakdown.
- If a partial rollback occurs, open an internal incident channel and post decision rationale.
- If engine enters conservative mode for Private installs, notify the customer's primary contact and record in audit log.
- Post-rollback: run targeted E2E prompts to determine root cause and add failing prompts to regression suite.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the decision engine; default to 'monitor-only' for first 48h
Enable automated graded rollback in Hosted for non-production orgs (canary sizes <= 5% traffic)
Enable for Dedicated pools with a guard: only pools marked 'auto-rollback-enabled'
Offer Private customers an opt-in adaptor (sidecar) and provide CLI to enable conservative mode
After 2 weeks of stable metrics and no false-positives, flip default to 'active' for new Hosted orgs
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Overreaction to noisy signals causing unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: hysteresis + require multiple metric windows and combine quality signals before action.
- Risk: Private customers cannot accept runtime mutators -> Mitigation: provide a shadow-only mode and manual operator guidance.
- Risk: Decision engine becomes single point of failure -> Mitigation: make decision engine stateless and replicable, with local fallback rules in adapters.
- Risk: False negatives (failures not rolled back) -> Mitigation: conservative default thresholds with escalation policy and human-in-loop overrides.
